newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Munich Re 1996/97 results please investors.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Munich Re 1996/97 results please investors.

text.p: Munich Re, the world's largest reinsurer, gave investors a fresh set of good news on Friday by reporting a bigger-than-expected rise in earnings per share for its 1996/97 year and proposing a dividend rise.

Munich Re shares jumped three percent to an all-time high of 6,135 marks after the results, which followed last week's announcement that it will strengthen its position in primary insurance with the merger of two affiliates, Victoria Holding AG and Hamburg-Mannheimer AG.
Munich Re also said it planned to raise its dividend by one mark to 17 marks, the fifth annual dividend rise in succession.
"This is further good news," said Georg Kanders, head of insurance research at Westdeutsche Landesbank. "The earnings per share figure was a positive surprise."

Preliminary figures showed earnings per share calculated according to DVFA standards -- the German Association of Financial Analysts and Investment Consultants -- rose to a record high 150 marks in the year ended June 30 after more than doubling to 140 marks in the previous year.
Analysts said the rise beat expectations after Munich Re had said last year it would be hard to match the record earnings achieved in 1995/96.
The rise in earnings per share (EPS) was explained by a heavy allocation to its claims equalisation provisions which was included in EPS, analysts said.
Group net profit rose more than 15 percent to just under 700 million marks ($400 million) from 595 million. The underwriting profit rose to about 800 million marks from 573 million marks.
Consolidated premium income increased 10 percent to 32 billion marks.

Excluding changes to the consolidated group in 1996/1997 -- when health insurer DKV Deutsche Krankenversicherung AG was consolidated for the first time and credit insurer Hermes Kreditversicherungs- AG left the consolidated group -- premium income rose three percent, Munich Re said.
Including American Re, whose acquisition was finalised last November and which will not be consolidated until the 1997/98 business year, Munich Re's premium income would total 38 billion marks.
The merger of Victoria and Hamburg-Mannheimer under the control of Munich Re will create ERGO Versicherungsgruppe, Germany's Number Two primary insurer.
It has yet to be approved by cartwel authorities and will be consolidated in the 1997/1998 accounts. If included now it would increase group premium income to 46.6 billion marks.

Group profit on investments rose to about 9.3 billion marks from 7.9 billion marks. The level of investments rose by 27 billion marks to 147 billion, due in part to favourable exchange rate movements, Munich Re said.

The group said it was able to maintain its position well in the reinsurance market in 1996/97 even though competition intensified. Gross reinsurance premiums rose by just under four percent to 19.2 billion marks.
Munich Re's primary insurance units saw premium income rise 23 percent to 12.8 billion marks. Most of the increase came from first-time consolidation.
The group also announced a 10-for-one stock split which will take place on August 18.
"This will make for cheaper custody and simpler trading of the registered shares, which account for more than 95 percent of Munich Re's share capital," Munich Re said in a statement.
The move means that based on Friday's record high, one share would be priced at 613.50 marks rather than 6,135 marks.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.753 German Marks)
